text:
jamie: Quick thought — we need to reconcile how pricing plan -> quota bucket mapping behaves during spikes. Current setup is per-org monthly cap + per-key RPM + per-key burst window. Proposal: introduce 'spike credits' to allow short bursts without immediate billing. Enforcement order idea: softcap notify -> spike credits -> hard throttle. Thoughts?

ryan: +1 on the softcap flow. Major decision: are spike credits per-key or per-org? Per-key is simpler for devs. Per-org smooths noisy keys but risks one key hogging pool.

sophia: I'm leaning per-org pool with per-key fair-share. Easier to manage backend state and we can tune fairness algorithm.

chris: SRE note — keeping tail latency predictable is priority. Per-org shared pools could let a large customer consume bursts and hurt others on same org. If we do shared pool, add reservation windows.

lena: Billing perspective — spike credits shouldn't be billed by default. If a customer exhausts monthly allotment and keeps using spike credits, we should have an opt-in automatic overage billing toggle for Pro/Enterprise. Need clear telemetry surfaced to customers.

mila: Telemetry needs: quota_used, spike_credit_used, throttle_events, overage_billed, per-key breakdown. Console should show both historical and realtime spike health.

ryan: Draft config example to make discussion concrete:

```
quota_mapping:
  free: {monthly_tokens:10000, rpm:60, spike_pool:1000, grace_days:7}
  pro: {monthly_tokens:5000000, rpm:600, spike_pool:50000, grace_days:14}
  enterprise: {monthly_tokens:unbounded, rpm:5000, spike_pool:200000, grace_days:30}
```

This is simplified but covers fields we need in the enforcement state machine.

jamie: UX idea — console should surface 'spike health' with predicted refill ETA and an option for enterprise to toggle 'charge on burst'. Also show X-Quota-Remaining headers in API response.

sophia: Enforcement precedence proposal: 1) per-key RPM floor (protect infra), 2) spike pool consumption (fair-share), 3) per-org softcap alerts (no throttle), 4) hard throttle / fallback routing to lower-cost model or queue.

chris: +1. Also add per-route throttle config so customers can prioritize critical routes. Fallback-routing to cheap model keeps service alive.

lena: For migrations: grandfather existing Pro customers for 60 days and emit clear emails + billing previews. We also need a per-org flag 'enforce_immediately' for when enterprise contracts require immediate cutoffs.

ryan: Operational question — do we stop accepting requests when monthly token budget is exceeded, or allow and bill later? I vote to reject (429) to protect capacity and make behavior deterministic. Soft-reject first, then hard.

jamie: Prefer soft-reject pattern: return 429 with headers: `X-Quota-Remaining`, `X-Spike-Credits`, and send webhook + console alert. That gives integrators a predictable signal.

mila: For console metrics: timeline chart for spike credit usage with per-key breakdown, plus a headline metric for percent_of_spike_pool_used. We'll need new indices and a tag schema to join keys -> orgs.

sophia: Implementation TODOs for infra: atomic decrement of spike pool across shards, fairness algorithm (weighted by key age/priority), tests for flash-surge fairness, and middleware hook for per-route decisions.

ryan: I'll draft an RFC with: config schema, enforcement state machine, telemetry contract, migration plan, and API header spec. Target: EOD Fri for initial draft.

jamie: Great — @lena please confirm billing knobs (grace_days, charge_on_burst, enforce_immediately) by Thursday so we can include them.

lena: Will confirm. One more ask: add `spike_decay_seconds` per-plan so we can define refill behavior.

dev-bot: Deploy status: quota-service/staging build 0.53.2 succeeded.

chris: Thanks all :thumbsup:
